newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end down on long liquidation.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end down on long liquidation.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended down on Tuesday on long liquidation, traders said.
The most actively traded September 1997 contract ended at 3,295 yuan ($397) per tonne, losing 88 yuan. It opened at 3,375 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 3,380 and a low of 3,290.
May fell 32 yuan to 3,265, July 40 to 3,260, November eight to 3,388 and the January 1998 contract 20 to 3,380 yuan.
Combined volume rose to 19,000 tonnes from 14,300 tonnes.
Most soybean contracts opened little changed from Monday's close but long liquidation pushed prices steadily down for most of the session.
Traders said long liquidation dominated Tuesday's trade with many investors cashing in their contracts to enter other active markets, including the bullish stock markets.
"A lack of market-moving news made many investors reluctant to hold onto their soybean futures positions," one trader said.
"The active stock markets attracted a great deal of hot money," he said.
Traders said they expect to see a technical rebound in soybeans in the next few days.
